minutes.headline: Task force leaned toward recommending an outside forensic audit of town finances and drafted override talking points.
minutes.summary: The Budget Task Force discussed hiring an outside forensic accounting firm via RFP to examine town finances, after the finance committee representative resigned. Members reviewed their punch list of savings and revenue ideas (shared services, busing, fees, cell towers, solar, CPA, health insurance), concluding none would close the gap alone. They agreed to prepare talking points for a special town meeting presentation, with no formal vote recorded.

public_comment.topic: Supports the task force's work; argues merging town and school facilities departments would give continuity and redundancy, cites Westford's single facilities department and permanent building committee; asked that someone track down the solar field question.

budget_items.what_was_said: Proposed as the number one recommendation; members noted the annual audit is higher level and does not dig into all accounts.
A member estimated hourly rates for a firm combining lawyers and accountants; concern about price tag.
Unexplained revenue category that vanished; described as several hundred thousand dollars.
Busing cost has risen steadily since 2021 with no state reimbursement for the non-regional district; options discussed included Fitchburg, owning buses.
Fees category rose substantially over several years; raising school fees tied to free and reduced lunch discussed as small revenue.
Phase one was not grant funded but units are rebate eligible; phase two grant planned for primary school.
Discussed as possible matching funds for building renovations; match has declined over the years.
Changing how warrants are mailed would require a charter change and save money.
Roughly 80 accounts, some returning nothing; prudent investor rule seen as best chance of improving outlook.

decisions.decision: Next meeting agenda: new finance committee rep, draft special town meeting talking points, and info on the town health insurance committee; two meetings remain before town meeting.
A member will email the finance committee alternate to ask whether she can step in.
A member will gather more forensic accounting firm names and check whether Lawrence did similar work; no formal commitment to issue an RFP was recorded.
Bullet-point talking points to be drafted and sent to Ezekiel beforehand; Ezekiel and the chair will divide who presents.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force leaned toward an outside forensic audit of town finances as its top recommendation, but took no vote and made no formal commitment to an RFP.
Members discussed hiring a firm that combines lawyers and accountants, noted the annual audit does not dig into all accounts, and worried about the price.
A member will gather more forensic accounting firm names and check whether Lawrence has done similar work.
Members reviewed savings and revenue ideas, including busing, fees, cell towers, solar, Community Preservation Act funds and health insurance, with no resolution on any.
Bullet-point talking points for the special town meeting will be drafted and sent ahead; the chair and Ezekiel will divide who presents.

why_it_matters: An outside audit, if pursued, would be a cost to the town and could shape what residents are told about the budget gap before they vote at the special town meeting.
None of the savings or revenue ideas discussed was shown to close the gap on its own, so the override framing being drafted is the part residents will most likely be asked to vote on.
